rule: These are demand anchors for prioritization and future corridor modelling. They do not create final Caribbean economics until route-level capture/fare assumptions are approved and country-reference rows are added.

source_claims: Tourism Analytics page cites Bahamas Ministry of Tourism, Nassau Lynden Pindling International Airport, and Central Bank sources.
Page contains CY2025 Bahamas air arrivals, cruise visitors by first port of entry, stopover visitors, and Nassau outbound revenue-generating passengers.
2019 baseline tables show 1,804,184 stopover visitors, 1,292,424 Nassau/Paradise Island stopovers, and 5,429,474 cruise visitors.
markets.model_use: Use Nassau/Paradise Island stopover + airport passenger + cruise first-port data as ceiling pools; derive corridor demand only after selecting concrete marina/resort routes.

source_claims: Puerto Rico Ferry lists San Juan ↔ Cataño as a 12-minute route.
Puerto Rico Ferry lists Ceiba ↔ Vieques as a 1-hour route.
Puerto Rico Ferry lists Ceiba ↔ Culebra as a 1-hour-30-minute route.
The service provides app-based ticket purchase, schedules, service alerts, and live ferry tracking.
markets.model_use: Use official ferry routes as exact corridor candidates; source passenger counts separately before economics.

source_claims: USVI Department of Tourism reported 303,388 total arrivals in Q1 2026, up 12% YoY and 6% over 2024.
March 2026 total arrivals were 121,716, up 23% YoY.
St. Thomas led Q1 growth with 246,772 arrivals; St. Croix recorded 56,616.
markets.model_use: Use as a tourism demand ceiling and prioritize St. Thomas/St. John/St. Croix route-specific ferry/charter passenger sourcing next.

source_claims: BTMI reports 503,000 stayover arrivals Jan-Aug 2025, up 5.43% YoY.
US became the top source market with 179,753 visitors Jan-Aug 2025; Caribbean source market had 70,984 visitors.
markets.model_use: Use as a high-priority app-mobility extension market; pair with Uber Barbados official launch and port modernization evidence before route economics.
